notes.meaning: Jesus, the Lamb of God, begins opening the seals of the scroll. As He breaks the first seal, one of the four living creatures calls out with a mighty voice like thunder, commanding the first horseman to come forth. Christ alone has the right to unfold God's secret plans for the world.

John sees a rider on a white horse holding a bow and wearing a victor's crown. In the traditional Protestant reading, this rider represents the pure gospel of Jesus Christ going out swiftly into all nations. The bow pictures God's word piercing hearts with conviction, and the crown shows that Christ's kingdom will surely triumph.

differ.view: Many evangelicals believe this rider is the antichrist, a deceptive world dictator who imitates Christ and brings a brief false peace before unleashing disaster.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Many modern scholars see the rider as a symbol of military conquest and human ambition in general, noting differences between this figure and Christ in Revelation 19.

notes.meaning: The Lamb breaks open the second seal of the heavenly scroll. The second living creature, which looks like an ox, calls out for the next judgment to appear. God's throne room directs each event that unfolds on the earth below.

A bright red horse gallops out, picturing the terrible judgment of war and bloodshed. God permits this rider to remove peace from the earth so that people butcher one another with a great sword. When people reject the peace of the gospel, God often hands them over to mutual destruction.

When the Lamb opens the third seal, the third living creature commands the next horseman to appear. John sees a black horse whose rider holds a pair of scales in his hand. The color black stands for deep mourning and distress, while the scales show that food has become so scarce it must be weighed out grain by grain.

A voice from among the living creatures announces severe prices for daily food. A worker's entire day of wages would buy only enough wheat to feed one person, or a small amount of coarse barley. The voice also commands that the olive trees and grapevines not be ruined, showing that God mercifully limits how far the shortage can go.

The Lamb opens the fourth seal of the scroll. The fourth living creature, which has the appearance of a flying eagle, summons the final horseman to ride forth. Heaven's authority guides every step of these earthly warnings.

A pale, sickly green horse appears, carrying a rider named Death, with the realm of the grave following right behind him. They are granted power over a fourth of the earth to kill by warfare, starvation, deadly disease, and wild beasts. These devastating plagues show the terrible wages of human rebellion against God.

When the fifth seal is opened, the scene shifts from earth to heaven, where John sees the souls of martyrs gathered under the altar. These believers had been put to death on earth because they held firmly to God's word and their witness for Christ. Though persecutors can destroy the body, they cannot harm the living soul in God's keeping.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic tradition sees the souls resting under heaven's altar as the spiritual pattern for placing the relics of holy martyrs inside or beneath church altars.

notes.meaning: The martyrs cry out loudly, asking their holy and true Master how long He will wait to judge the earth and avenge their blood. This prayer is not born of hateful revenge, but of a deep desire to see God's justice vindicated and evil stopped. God's people can safely leave all vengeance in His hands.

Each martyr receives a bright white robe as a gift, symbolizing innocence, holiness, and victory. They are told to rest in peace a little longer until the full, appointed number of their fellow servants who will be killed is complete. God has an exact count of His witnesses and will not let their suffering be in vain.

The opening of the sixth seal brings violent cosmic upheaval. A massive earthquake shakes the world, the sun turns completely black like rough sackcloth, and the full moon appears blood red. These shocking signs show that the old world order is shaking apart before the majesty of God.

John sees the stars falling from the sky to the earth like unripe figs shaken loose by a mighty gale. This vivid picture illustrates how easily human rulers and proud earthly powers will be cast down from their heights. Nothing made by man can hold its place against the power of God.

The visible sky rolls away out of sight like an old scroll being rolled up and set aside. Every mountain and island is shaken out of its normal spot by the violent changes taking place. The things people thought were most solid and permanent on earth will give way before the Lord.

Panic spreads across every level of society, from ruling kings, high officials, and wealthy men down to soldiers, slaves, and free citizens. All of them rush into dark mountain caves and among the rocks to hide from impending ruin. In the hour of divine judgment, worldly wealth and status cannot save anyone.

The terrified people plead with the mountains and rocks to collapse on them. They would rather be crushed to death than face the holy presence of God on His throne and the righteous anger of the Lamb. Those who despised the gentle Savior now experience the terror of His divine wrath.

The trembling crowds cry out that the great day of divine wrath has finally arrived. They ask who can possibly survive or stand justified before the holy Judge. Without the pardon found in Jesus Christ, no sinner can withstand that final day of reckoning.
